Baligrod Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Baligród, Poland

Not demolished. Baligród's Jewish population peaked in the interwar period at 1,000 people (58 percent of the town) in 1930. This cemetery, established at least as early as the mid-17th century, was devastated during WWII, its matzevot used to harden the surface of the market square, where fragments remain beneath a newer layer today. About 300 tombstones survive in their original places, arranged in traditional rows divided by sex; the oldest is dated 1716, with several damaged stones likely from the 17th century. The cemetery was entered into the Register of Monuments in 1990.
